q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of rubber hose per metre?
title: Rubber hose carbon footprint per metre
short: Add the rubber compound, textile or wire reinforcement per metre and multiply each by its supplier figure. Then add mixing, extrusion and steam curing energy, and divide the plant's energy by metres of hose dispatched.
audience: Rubber hose makers for agriculture, industry and automobiles

ul: Natural and synthetic rubber, carbon black and oils by weight.
Polyester or nylon braid, or steel wire reinforcement.
Steam autoclave curing from a boiler.

p: Report per metre by bore size and ply. Larger bores and wire reinforced hoses carry much more material per metre.

example.title: Worked example: rubber hose unit per metre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 66,150 / 150,000 = 0.441 kg CO2 per metre
Add rubber compound and reinforcement for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
